source: CARDI book "ដំណាំស្រូវនៅកម្ពុជា" (Rice Cultivation in Cambodia), by Men Sarom, Thuy Lina and Pheng Thimuny, published by CARDI, 2007, Chapter 9 (Harmful factors and management), sections 9.2.1 (Sap-sucking insects) and 9.2.2 (Stem/leaf-feeding insects). No elibrary URL visible.
text: This source names several rice-associated pest species not clearly documented elsewhere in the existing knowledge base, in addition to the well-covered leaffolder/stem borer/rice bug/golden apple snail/rat entries: (1) Root aphid (Tetraneura nigriabdominalis) and a related root/shoot-feeding aphid (Rhopalosiphum rufiabdominalis), Hemiptera: Aphididae - these live on rice roots below the soil surface and are frequently tended/farmed by the fire ant Solenopsis geminata, which protects the aphids from predators in exchange for their sugary secretions. (2) Fire ant (ស្រមោចភ្លើង, Solenopsis geminata Fabricius, Hymenoptera: Formicidae) - in addition to farming root aphids, this ant can directly damage rice by carrying away newly-sown or germinating seed, particularly a concern during direct-seeding establishment; management is mainly by disturbing/destroying nest mounds near seeded fields and by seed treatment with a systemic insecticide. (3) Green stink bug (ស្រីងជញ្ជក់បេះង, Nezara viridula Linnaeus, Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) - a grain-sucking bug distinct from the already-documented rice bug (Leptocorisa oratorius); feeds on developing grain causing discoloration and empty/partially-filled kernels, and is a general crop pest not specific to rice. (4) Zigzag leafhopper (មមាចញ្ចោស, Recilia dorsalis, Homoptera: Cicadellidae) - named as another leafhopper capable of transmitting rice virus diseases, distinguished from the green leafhopper implicated in tungro transmission; identifiable by a pale zigzag ('Z') marking on the wing. (5) Skipper/leaf-rolling caterpillars (ដង្កូវព័ទ្ធស្លឹក, Pelopidas mathias and Parnara guttata, Lepidoptera: Hesperiidae) - fold and feed on rice leaves in a manner visually similar to the already-documented rice leaffolder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis, Lepidoptera: Pyralidae) but belonging to a different insect family; generally considered a less damaging, secondary defoliator.
caveat: These are minor/secondary pests relative to the major species already thoroughly documented in the knowledge base (leaffolder, stem borer, rice bug, golden apple snail, rats, thrips, caseworm). Recommend a duplicate-check before final inclusion, since this session had no repo access to confirm these aren't already covered under a general 'other pests' entry. This entry does not include chemical control recommendations for most of these species since the source's treatment of them was brief and not clearly separated from surrounding pest-group text.
